project.name: deck
project.summary: A generic, config-driven hub engine — the single human entry point to a home-lab estate: launch portal with service status, inventory beside reality (drift and coverage), and a monitoring overview, with slots for governed actions and in-deck docs/configs.

audiences.name: Estate operator
audiences.description: Runs deck against their own home-lab estate: authors the estate config repo, deploys deck, wires monitoring, and keeps the observed-reality snapshot fresh. Comfortable with YAML, Docker, and a terminal; not a deck contributor.

audiences.name: Engine maintainer
audiences.description: Works on deck's own code — the schema, server, providers, drift engine, and web app. Needs the architecture spine and the internal HTTP contract.

audiences.name: Module author
audiences.description: Extends deck beyond config: writes a sidecar in any language, a module built into deck, or a runtime module loaded from DECK_MODULES_DIR. Comfortable with HTTP/JSON, and for in-process modules with TypeScript and React; not necessarily a deck maintainer.

sources.note: The `deck` bin: `validate` and `render` subcommands, arg parsing, exit classes (0 clean / 1 findings / 2 tool error).
Server boot: load config, resolve sources+actions runtimes, register providers, start poll scheduler, build Hono app, serve under Bun. Fail-fast on bad config.
React SPA. Feature auto-discovery via registry; registered nav: home, portal, hosts, services, docs, monitoring, drift, actions (+ detail routes).
Real workspace commands: dev, start, build, test, typecheck, snapshot:example. Bun runs server+schema from TS source; only web is built.
@deck/schema public exports: validate, validateSnapshot, merge, classify, KNOWN_PROVIDER_KINDS, and all config/snapshot/findings types. JSON Schemas are authoritative; .ts types are generated.

Authoritative estate-config shape: required schemaVersion(1)+estate; optional hosts/services/groups/sources/integrations/actions/agents/llmUsage. Defines Source (incl. credentialEnv = env-var NAME), Integration, Action, LlmUsage.
Authoritative observed-reality contract: ObservedHost/Service, coverage (collected|partial|unreachable), DriftFinding, Waiver, generatedAt.
Config dir resolution (--config / $DECK_CONFIG_DIR / ./config), lexical *.yaml layering (00-base before 10-overlay), YAML→merge→validate, canonicalization.
Rule-based validator: identity, layers, provider-kinds, references, secrets, types, version. Findings + exit classification.
HTTP route table (/api/config, /api/providers[/:id], /api/health, /api/sources/:id/{tree,file,raw,search}, /api/actions*) and the typed @deck/server contract barrel consumed by the web app.

11 provider kinds — alertmanager, docker, file-tree, gatus, http-health, http-json, link, markdown-tree, prometheus, remote, snapshot — plus registry (register/read/startScheduler/listHealth) and wiring (registerAllProviders).
Server-derived drift/coverage projection: deriveDriftProjection, filters, evidence, ordering, coverage rows/counts, severities, waiver state.
Read-only source browsing: tree/file/raw/search, path confinement (confine.ts), git acquisition + on-disk cache, capability gating (SOURCE_NOT_FOUND when off).
LLM usage collector: Claude statusLine/OAuth/transcripts and Codex app-server/rollout sources, adaptive cadence with the 2-minute OAuth floor, /api/llm-usage routes and the ingest bearer gate.
Governed actions: executor, runner allowlist, param validation, audit store, run events. Capability OFF by default; routes 403 until enabled.
Secret-reference model: credentialEnv holds an env-var NAME (pattern ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$), never a value; suspected-secret detection in validation.
Freshness model (FreshnessStamp/State, ProviderEnvelope) and deriveState; snapshotStaleAfter drives host freshness.
DECK_* env vars: CONFIG_DIR, PORT, SNAPSHOT_SOURCE, WEB_DIST, LOG_LEVEL, SOURCES_CACHE_DIR, ACTIONS_ENABLED, DATA_DIR, RUNNERS_FILE, ACTION_TIMEOUT_MS.

Playwright operator flows (inventory, drift, actions, alerts, sources). start-inventory-api.ts is the canonical full-engine wiring: build config/overlay/snapshot scenario, boot(), materialize source fixtures.
HTTP integration tests (provider-routes, alerts-routes, sources-routes) — verified request/response usage.
Validation/merge/ownership behavior with rich valid + invalid fixtures — ground truth for what a well-formed estate/snapshot is.
Worked estate: 00-base + 10-overlay YAML, configs/, docs/, snapshot.template.json; reference docker-compose mounting ./estate:/config:ro.
Multi-stage build (node:22 builder → oven/bun runtime), single Bun process serves web+API, container defaults (/config, :8080), HEALTHCHECK on /api/health, snapshot templating at boot.
Jobs: node-pnpm (typecheck+unit), web-e2e (sharded Playwright), bun-parity (vitest under Bun), gates (golden render, boot smoke).

The module contract: ModuleManifest (identity, enabledBy, env, config, providerKinds, services, contributes, health, dataDir), the ServerModuleContext services, defineServerModule/defineWebModule, the UI id/slot/path rules and DECK_API_VERSION 0.1.0.

Module host: runtime module loading, config composition, planning (enable, order, refuse), init with an injected context, route mounting; BUILTIN_MODULES (19 built-ins); KERNEL_PATHS and the no-feature-names guard.
composeConfig: the kernel schema plus module sections, per-kind instance schemas, ownership, identity, unique, references and finding codes; deck validate composes the same way.

UI manifest resolution (GET /api/ui): extension tree, ui config overrides, config pages, widget types, status maps, hot reload (live.ts), sidecar pages; built-ins' shared UI contributions and the core slots and widget types.
Web half registration (registerWebModule), runtime web halves over the import map, @deck/sdk, the TanStack Query data layer, config pages and the core widget renderers.
The runtime module template (hello) and example (maintenance), the NUT UPS sidecar, the no-code dashboard overlay, and the @deck/sdk build-time package (types, Tailwind preset, deck-module lint).
The remote provider protocol v1: data and describe endpoints, describe validation (widget allowlist, bounds, link and markdown policy), sidecar pages and findings.
Design decisions recorded during the forge pipeline — the why behind runtime, config layering, and the two-document model. Provenance for proposed ADRs; not user docs.

gaps.note: docs/initial-release-plan.md (~425 lines) is a release-planning artifact, not product documentation. It is intentionally excluded from the corpus (like specs/); do not fold it into a user-facing doc.

g-providers (RESOLVED during drafting): per-kind config was read from each provider's index.ts. Verified structure now in r3/h2 — integration-backed kinds are docker/gatus/prometheus/alertmanager (register under a fixed id equal to their kind; only the first integration of each kind is polled; credentialEnv is sent verbatim as the Authorization header); source-backed kinds are file-tree/markdown-tree; http-health and link are host/service BINDING kinds (http-health has url/method, no credentialEnv); snapshot is a runtime singleton fed by DECK_SNAPSHOT_SOURCE.

g-git-auth (RESOLVED during drafting): verified in sources/acquire.ts. Token applies to HTTPS remotes only, sent as Authorization: Basic base64('x-access-token:<token>') via GIT_CONFIG_* env for the clone spawn only (never in URL/argv, so never persisted to .git/config); ssh remotes ignore it; a named-but-unset var yields an unauthenticated clone. h7 is written as fact.

g-http-health-known-kinds (RESOLVED): confirmed bug — http-health is a real host/service binding kind (collectBinding in apps/server/src/providers/index.ts) but was omitted from KNOWN_PROVIDER_KINDS, so an http-health binding drew a spurious PROVIDER_KIND_UNKNOWN warning. Fixed: added http-health to the registry and CONTRACT.md, covered it in the primary fixture + golden render, and added a regression test.

g-example-monitoring: the bundled example estate declares no integrations, so the monitoring surface renders an empty 'no backends' state; the tutorial (t1) says so and does not claim monitoring is populated by the example.

g-sources-flag: there is no global sources enable/disable env flag (unlike actions). The capability activates by declaring a supported-kind source; gating is per-source (unknown id → 404). h3 documents this per-source activation rather than a switch. DECK_SOURCES_CACHE_DIR only affects git-repo sources.

g-confirm-enforcement (RESOLVED): Action.confirm has no server-side enforcement in modules/actions/server/ — it is a UI-only affordance. Maintainer confirmed UI-only is intended (not a server guarantee). Documented as such in h4 (governed-actions guide) and r1 (estate-config reference); no code change.

g-snapshot-out: DECK_SNAPSHOT_OUT is a real env var read by docker/entrypoint.sh (default /tmp/deck/snapshot.json) to redirect where the templated example snapshot is materialized. It is entrypoint-only (not read by boot.ts) and was missing from the s-env enumeration; add it to r4 as a container-entrypoint convenience var.

g-topology: Deployment is self-hosted Docker/compose with an operator-provided authenticating reverse proxy. There is no published-registry/release workflow and no infrastructure-as-code, so proxy/network topology is operator-specific and shown as an external boundary, not asserted.

g-adr: No ADRs exist under docs/. adr1–adr3 propose formalizing decisions whose mechanism is observable in code; their rationale lives in specs/deck/charter/01-decisions.md and forge-decisions.json. Confirm intent with the maintainer before publishing them as settled records.

Architecture notes exist for only 3 of the ~7 shipped features (hosts-and-services, governed-actions, sources-docs-and-configs). Drift-and-coverage, alerts-and-health, portal, and engine-core have none; bb1 is planned as the connecting spine rather than one note per feature, to keep the architecture set at a surviving altitude.

The HTTP API (r6) is an internal, proxy-fronted surface consumed by the bundled web app, not a committed public API. It should be documented as internal/subject-to-change, not as a stability contract.
